rows.label: Concept
rows.text: Animals are tailored to their habitats as plants are. Aquatic animals — primary like fish with gills, fins and swim bladders, or secondary like whales that returned with lungs — solve buoyancy and oxygen; terrestrial animals solve drying with waterproof skins, internal fertilisation and lungs.…

rows.label: Formula
rows.text:
Aquatic: fusiform body + fins + gills (countercurrent) + lateral line + webbed feet
Terrestrial: waterproof skin + lungs + internal fertilisation + strong limbs
Volant: wings + hollow bones + air sacs + strong pectoral muscles + streamlined body + beak

rows.label: Conditions
rows.text: **Primary vs secondary aquatic animals:** primary (fish) evolved in water with gills; secondary (whale, seal) evolved on land, breathe lungs, return to water.  ·  **Adaptation vs acclimatisation:** adaptation is inherited (evolutionary); acclimatisation is a short-term physiological adjustment within an individual's lifetime.

rows.label: Special cases
rows.text: NEB expects a clear aquatic (primary + secondary), terrestrial (cursorial, fossorial, arboreal), and volant adaptation list.  ·  Countercurrent exchange in fish gills is a very common exam point.

rows.label: Solved
rows.text: ***Horse*** — cursorial: single hoofed digit, long limbs.  ·  ***Mole*** — fossorial: spade-like forelimbs, reduced eyes.

rows.label: Quick concepts
rows.text: **Adaptation is inherited, acclimatisation is not:** the 2023 MCQ point — inherited modifications are adaptations; lifetime physiological adjustments are acclimatisation.

rows.label: Key points
rows.text: Habitat = address; niche = profession. Biotic: producers, consumers, decomposers; abiotic: light, temperature, water, soil.  ·  Aquatic: streamlined body, gills/swim bladder, fins; secondary aquatic (whale) keep lungs.  ·  Terrestrial: cursorial (long limbs, reduced digits — horse), fossorial (claws, reduced eyes — mole), arboreal (opposable thumbs, prehensile tail, binocular vision), volant (wings, hollow bones, keel — birds; patagium — bat).  ·  Population: natality +, mortality −, density = individuals/area; growth = (natality + immigration) − (mortality + emigration).

rows.label: Universal facts
rows.text: Birds' hollow (pneumatic) bones and keeled sternum cut weight while anchoring flight muscles — weight is the enemy of flight.

rows.text: ## 1. Topic Introduction — Animals Tailored to Their Habitats Like plants, animals evolve body plans and behaviours matched to their habitats.
